stories.title: Quinn Emanuel wins fraud case against healthcare founder
Parole Board invites public to observe
Freeths strengthens team with ten new lawyers
stories.ltme_summary: Freeths has added ten lawyers to its Employment, Pensions and Immigration team across seven of its twelve offices. National head Rena Magdani says revenue in the team has risen 85 per cent over five years. The firm is also preparing a 2027 Employment Survey covering employment law reform and AI in the workplace.
stories.hook: Freeths adds ten lawyers to employment team, citing 85 per cent revenue growth

stories.title: Addleshaw Goddard forms AI collaboration
stories.ltme_summary: Addleshaw Goddard has announced a strategic partnership with Harvey to deploy AI across its workforce of more than 3,400 professionals in Europe, the Middle East and Asia, from January. The firm's 80-member Innovation Group says it tested several platforms over three months. The two firms will co-develop tools, and the firm says the work has already produced Review Tables.
stories.hook: Addleshaw Goddard signs Harvey for firmwide AI from January, with joint product work

stories.title: Fiona McNulty leads Law Society poll
stories.hook: Mason Hayes & Curran's Fiona McNulty tops Law Society of Ireland council poll again

stories.title: Second Circuit Denies Injunction Pending Appeal in Docket 26-1835
Legal sector jobs hit record high in October, new data shows
stories.ltme_summary: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics data, as reported by Law360, shows legal sector employment reached a record 1,251,200 in October. That is 2,400 more than in September and 22,800 more year on year. The ABA Journal reports the figures, which are seasonally adjusted. The page also shows a wider jobs figure for the US economy.
stories.hook: US legal sector employment hits record 1.25 million in October, BLS data shows

stories.title: Sheppard mandates four day per week return to office
Todd Blanche Is The Real Victim. Just Ask Him, He’ll Tell You!
CVS Health Bids Goodbye To Vertical Integration But Not Conflict Of Interest
Addleshaw Goddard Picks Harvey, Fieldfisher Opts For Legora
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer reports that Addleshaw Goddard has chosen Harvey firmwide and will co-develop features, while Fieldfisher has picked Legora after a six-week pilot with 137 users. Fieldfisher has 1,400 lawyers and staff and will lead the rollout from its AI hub in Berlin. Fieldfisher says it will keep building its own AI capabilities.
stories.hook: Fieldfisher picks Legora after six-week pilot as Addleshaw Goddard chooses Harvey

stories.title: UK judge instructs expert witnesses to be transparent about AI use
stories.ltme_summary: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith has told expert witnesses to disclose any material use of AI in their reports, according to statements carried by the Law Society Gazette. The instruction follows a Civil Justice Council working group report recommending a disclosure rule. Smith cited Cornwall Council v M & Ors [2026] EWFC 306, where a judge gave little weight to a report produced with Microsoft Copilot.
stories.hook: Joanna Smith tells experts to disclose AI use after Copilot-drafted report is discounted

stories.title: CBABC invites dialogue with new BC government on Legal Professions Act
stories.ltme_summary: The Canadian Bar Association's British Columbia branch has invited dialogue with the new provincial government on the Legal Professions Act. Its president, Connor Bildfell, said lawyers must stay self-regulated. The Act, passed in 2024, is tied up in litigation, and the Conservatives have committed to repealing it, according to the statement.
stories.hook: CBA British Columbia asks new government to talk before any repeal of the Legal Professions Act

stories.title: Legaltech Hub CEO Joins Davis Polk As AI Chief
stories.ltme_summary: Law360 Pulse reports that the chief executive of Legaltech Hub has moved to Davis Polk as its AI chief. The report is a short outlet summary line, so the role and timing come from the headline alone. It matches the departure announced by LawSites and LawNext.
stories.hook: Legaltech Hub chief executive joins Davis Polk as AI chief, Law360 Pulse reports

stories.title: Quinn Emanuel Secures Judgment In USD 5 Billion Fraud Claim Against NMC Health’s Founder and Former CEO, Weeks After USD 600m Bank of Baroda Settlement
From Sidley Associate to Capitol Hill: Melat Kiros Makes History as First Gen Z Woman Elected to Congress
New Zealand Slips in Global Rule of Law Rankings as Australia and Britain Also Fall
Founder Nikki Shaver to Leave Legaltech Hub, Investor Jeroen Plink to Step In, Announces Strategic Partnership with Baretz+Brunelle
stories.ltme_summary: Legaltech Hub chief executive Nikki Shaver will leave the company on 1 December to join Davis Polk as chief AI and knowledge officer, according to LawSites. Investor Jeroen Plink will become chief executive. The company also announced a strategic partnership with Baretz+Brunelle and its LexFusion arm, which the parties describe as a growth partnership. Baretz told LawSites it was not a prelude to an acquisition.
stories.hook: Legaltech Hub's Nikki Shaver leaves for Davis Polk; Baretz+Brunelle forms partnership

stories.title: Kindleworth targets US Big Law breakaways with New York launch
stories.ltme_summary: Kindleworth, a consultancy that helps lawyers set up their own firms, has launched in New York. It says it has helped establish more than 50 legal businesses since 2012. The launch targets US partners leaving large firms. The extract is a short opening with a sidebar of other headlines, so the details of the office are limited to what is shown.
stories.hook: Kindleworth opens in New York to help US Big Law partners set up their own firms

stories.title: More than 50 laterals in a year: the thinking behind Dechert’s growth blueprint
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports on Dechert's year of lateral hiring, with more than 50 laterals in 2026, and sets out the strategy from its co-chairs. The article is listed in the extract, but its body is not visible, so the firm's account of its strategy is not confirmed here.
stories.hook: Dechert reports more than 50 lateral hires in a year under its growth plan

stories.title: Top City law firm partner warns aspiring lawyers against ‘AI inflation’ on CVs
stories.ltme_summary: A White & Case global M&A partner, Ferdinand Mason, has warned law students against overstating AI-assisted experience on training contract applications. Speaking through a LinkedIn post reported by Legal Cheek, he said some applicants claimed multi-billion pound deal work after short vacation schemes. He advised candidates to describe their real tasks and what they learned, and to use AI only to tidy drafts.
stories.hook: White & Case partner tells students AI-inflated CVs will not impress recruiters

stories.title: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader claims first as pro bono becomes part of partnership rulebook
Monday morning round-up
Harvey IPO: The question isn’t really if it wants to float, but should it?
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider has published a commentary asking whether Harvey should float on the stock market, rather than whether it wants to. The extract is only a verification page, so the argument cannot be assessed here. Harvey has reportedly held early IPO talks, as covered in other stories this week.
stories.hook: Harvey's IPO question is whether it should float, not whether it wants to

stories.title: Nikki Shaver departs Legaltech Hub to become Davis Polk’s chief AI officer
stories.ltme_summary: Nikki Shaver is leaving Legaltech Hub, where she is chief executive, to become chief AI officer at Davis Polk. The extract is only a verification page, so the start date and role title rest on the headline. The Legaltech Hub account of the move is covered in a separate story from another outlet.
stories.hook: Nikki Shaver moves from Legaltech Hub to Davis Polk as chief AI officer

stories.title: Addleshaw Goddard selects Harvey for firmwide rollout and product collaboration
stories.hook: Addleshaw Goddard picks Harvey firmwide and will help build its features

stories.title: Kindleworth takes its law firm launch playbook to New York
stories.ltme_summary: Kindleworth has opened a New York office, appointing Maryana Kodner as partner and head of US operations and recruiting Anand David as a strategic adviser. The consultancy says it has supported more than 50 law firm launches and has 60 staff. CEO James Hacking says New York is the natural next step, following a 2025 minority investment from Burford Capital.
stories.hook: Kindleworth opens New York office with Maryana Kodner as US operations head

stories.title: Addleshaw Goddard becomes latest firm to co-develop Harvey tools
stories.ltme_summary: Addleshaw Goddard will work with Harvey's product and engineering teams to develop AI tools and will roll Harvey out to more than 3,400 lawyers and business services staff. Nonbillable says other firms are doing similar co-development deals, including Latham, Freshfields and Pinsent Masons. It also reports that Harvey plans to offer the Latham fund formation tool to other firms.
stories.hook: Addleshaw Goddard joins firms co-developing Harvey tools, Nonbillable reports

stories.title: City law partner calls out AI-driven CV inflation
The realities of scaling AI agents: ‘You don't have an AI problem, you have a content problem’
stories.ltme_summary: Sifted, in partnership with Box, reports a panel discussion on scaling autonomous AI agents safely. Panellists from Deliverance AI, Box, Ralio and Geordie AI argued for staged access, zero-trust design and early involvement of governance teams. Box's solutions engineer said clean, well-organised content is the main barrier to reliable agent use.
stories.hook: Sifted panel says AI agents need staged access and clean content before deployment

stories.title: Needs remain unmet despite greater sector transparency
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board says a poll of 10,000 small businesses found about 11 per cent had a legal need requiring professional help, and eight in ten of them went unmet. Shopping around rose by 19 percentage points since 2021. Chatbots were a source of help for 6 per cent of businesses, and 15 per cent had used AI for legal advice.
stories.hook: Small firms shop around more for lawyers, yet eight in ten legal needs go unmet

stories.title: Solicitor refused five-and-a-half year extension to appeal SDT findings
stories.ltme_summary: The High Court refused solicitor Zeeshan Mian an extension of time to appeal findings by the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal. The appeal was filed in September 2025, more than five and a half years after the deadline. Robert Palmer KC, sitting as a deputy High Court judge, called the delay serious and significant. Mian was fined £20,000 and ordered to pay £25,000 costs.
stories.hook: High Court refuses solicitor's appeal filed more than five years out of time

stories.title: CPS stalking cases missing vital risk assessments, inspectors find
stories.ltme_summary: HM Crown Prosecution Service Inspectorate found that prosecutors were too often not given risk assessments and victim personal statements in stalking cases. Of 348 cases, risk assessments were present in 245. Inspectors agreed with the chosen charge in 76.6 per cent of 308 cases. The report is 122 pages and makes recommendations to the CPS.
stories.hook: Inspectors find CPS stalking files often lack risk assessments and victim statements

stories.title: ‘Dieselgate’ quantum trial begins over Mercedes defeat devices
stories.ltme_summary: The quantum trial in the Pan-NOx 'dieselgate' group litigation began, focusing on Mercedes-Benz vehicles found to contain defeat devices. The trial is before Mr Justice Constable and is listed to end before Christmas. The court will decide the value of claims against Mercedes, which denies that claimants suffered loss.
stories.hook: Dieselgate quantum trial opens against Mercedes ahead of Christmas finish

stories.title: 'How on earth?' Bar leader questions lack of senior black judges
stories.ltme_summary: Keir Monteith KC, founding chair of the Criminal Bar Association's Black Barristers' Committee, questioned the absence of a Black judge in the Court of Appeal or Supreme Court. He spoke at the committee's launch in London to around 350 people. Shami Chakrabarti also spoke, arguing that the senior judiciary has never had enough judges of colour.
stories.hook: Criminal Bar Association committee questions absence of Black judges in top courts

stories.title: ‘Give your opinion, not someone else’s,’ Post Office Inquiry counsel tells experts
stories.ltme_summary: Emma Price of 5 Essex Chambers, counsel to the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry, told experts at the Bond Solon Expert Witness Conference that they must give their own opinions and not let others edit their reports. She discussed Fujitsu engineer Gareth Jenkins's evidence. The inquiry's final volumes, covering lawyers' roles, are expected soon.
stories.hook: Post Office inquiry counsel tells experts to hold the pen on their own reports

stories.title: Policy paper: Courts and Tribunals Bill
stories.ltme_summary: The government introduced the Courts and Tribunals Bill to Parliament, according to HM Courts and Tribunals Service and the Ministry of Justice. The bill proposes removing defendants' right to elect Crown Court trial in triable-either-way cases, creating a Bench Division, and allowing trial by judge alone for some complex fraud cases. The page was updated on 9 November 2026 with a new impact document.
stories.hook: Government's Courts and Tribunals Bill would end defendants' election for Crown Court trial

stories.title: Decision: Gangmasters Licensing Appeals results and judgements
stories.ltme_summary: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has updated its table of Gangmasters Licensing Appeals results, dated 9 November 2026. The appeals concern decisions of the Gangmasters and Labour Abuse Authority, which closed in April 2026 with its functions passed to the Fair Work Agency. The page sets out the appeal rights that remain for licence refusals and conditions.
stories.hook: Gangmasters licence appeal results updated as Fair Work Agency takes over functions

stories.title: Legal problems are holding back small business growth, new survey finds
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board says its Small Business Legal Needs Survey, based on more than 10,000 small businesses, found that 36 per cent had at least one legal issue last year. It estimates around 16 million legal issues a year across England and Wales. Late payment is singled out as a damaging problem, and nearly one in five businesses said legal issues had delayed investment.
stories.hook: Legal Services Board survey puts small business legal issues at 16 million a year
entities: Office of the Small Business Commissioner

stories.title: ILTA and Thomson Reuters Institute Release AI Guide for Transactional Legal Professionals
stories.hook: ILTA and Thomson Reuters Institute publish AI guide for deal lawyers covering the transaction lifecycle

stories.hook: Davis Polk hires Legaltech Hub co-founder Nikki Shaver as its first chief AI and knowledge officer

stories.title: AI Makes Contracting Faster Yet Businesses Are Struggling to Show the ROI
Back to Brains: Filevine’s Michael Anderson on Smart Pens, Voice Agents, and Getting Lawyers Off the Keyboard
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor interviews Michael Anderson, Filevine's chief product officer, at the LEX Summit. Topics include the LOIS smart pen, a citator with semantic Shepardising, a deposition marketplace acquisition and voice agents that answer firm calls. Anderson says attorneys have adopted AI faster than expected.
stories.hook: Filevine's Michael Anderson unveils a smart pen and voice intake agents at LEX Summit

stories.title: LSAC president Sudha Setty reflects on dynamic landscape of law school admissions
The Burton Book Review: ‘All We Say’ by Ben Rhodes
The Next Law School Admissions Crisis Could Be About Loans
It All Hinges On Judgment: The Work Not Counted
The Best Law Schools For Criminal Law (2026)
Legendary Litigator Who Took On Trump Passes Away While Prepping For Trial
For Access To Justice, The Perfect Lawyer Is The Enemy Of The Good Chatbot
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports on remarks by former Legal Services Corporation president Jim Sandman at the Everlaw Summit in San Francisco. Sandman, who now teaches at the University of South Carolina, says AI chatbots could help people with everyday legal problems by pointing them to non-court steps first, whereas legal research tools were accurate but poor at communicating. He concedes frontier models still sometimes get the law wrong.
stories.hook: Jim Sandman says chatbots may keep tenants out of court, but accuracy still lags behind plain-language advice

stories.title: A Proof Of Concept Is A Question, Not A Product
Blackletter Bags $6m for Transactional New Mod
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer reports that Blackletter, a US AI-native law firm, has raised $6m in a seed round led by Lerer Hippeau. The firm focuses on M&A, finance and other complex work, and says it has seven lawyers so far. Co-founder and CEO Jonathan Rosenbluth says the firm does not use billable hours and runs its own AI operating system, BlackletterOS.
stories.hook: Blackletter raises $6m seed led by Lerer Hippeau to take complex M&A and finance work with AI-native model

stories.title: Long waits, real consequences: the legal implications of Canada's ER delays
AI Provider EvenUp Hires Ex-Vanta Chief Revenue Officer
Small business legal needs remain unmet despite greater transparency
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board says a poll of 10,000 small businesses found about 11 per cent had a legal need requiring professional help, and eight in 10 of them did not have it met. The regulator says 48 per cent of businesses facing a legal issue shopped around for a provider, up 19 percentage points since 2021. Chatbots were a source of help for 6 per cent of businesses.
stories.hook: Legal Services Board finds eight in 10 small businesses with a professional legal need went unmet despite easier price checks

stories.title: How to improve client onboarding with remote identity verification
Legal Ethics Roundup: DOJ Ethics Probe, Bar Exam Tampering, AI Billing Limits, TX Reconsiders ABA Accreditation Council, Biglaw Shakeup, AI Privilege & More
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law's weekly ethics roundup by Renee Knake Jefferson covers several items, including a federal judge's plan to appoint a special master over Justice and Interior Department lawyers in a golf course case, criminal charges over tampered Arkansas bar exam results, and a New York State Bar Association call to restrict billing for AI time savings. The newsletter also covers Texas moves on ABA accreditation. Much of the content is legal ethics rather than technology.
stories.hook: New York State Bar Association tells lawyers not to bill clients for time saved by AI

stories.title: John Fetterman And Other Losers On Election Day
Addleshaw Goddard, Harvey Partner On Firmwide AI Adoption
stories.ltme_summary: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech reports a headline that Addleshaw Goddard and Harvey are working together on firmwide AI adoption. The item is a single summary line with no article text in the extract, so the scope of the arrangement is not visible here.
stories.hook: Addleshaw Goddard and Harvey are working on firmwide AI adoption, according to Law360 Pulse

stories.title: How It Works: A Look Inside iManage’s Next-Generation Platform and Its New AI Capabilities
stories.ltme_summary: LawNext presents a sponsored demonstration of iManage's next-generation document and email platform, with new AI tools for meeting preparation, document enrichment, comparison and tabular review. iManage says existing customers can adopt the new experience without migrating documents. Paul Walker, iManage's global solutions director, walks through the features.
stories.hook: iManage shows its next-generation platform, with AI meeting briefings and document review, in a sponsored demo

stories.title: First satisfied client for groundbreaking technology-only law firm
stories.hook: LawFairy says its deterministic tool fixed a wrongly filed UK visa case, then handed it to Setfords for approval

stories.title: Family law AI tools “could make conflict worse”
stories.ltme_summary: Dr Natalie Byrom's report for the Nuffield Family Justice Observatory warns that generative AI tools could make family disputes worse by encouraging intransigence. It says the LawtechUK tracker lists eight family law providers, of which only three plausibly offer dispute resolution. The report also says the judiciary uses a secure Microsoft Copilot without published monitoring.
stories.hook: Byrom report warns family law AI tools could make conflict worse and says judges' Copilot use lacks published oversight

stories.title: Why State AI Laws Are Piling Up | Insights & Resources | Goodwin
stories.ltme_summary: Goodwin's Forces of Law podcast features Gabe Maldoff discussing the growing patchwork of US state AI laws, despite federal deregulatory moves under the Trump administration. Maldoff says thousands of state bills have been proposed and the number of enacted laws has grown in the past year. The episode was recorded before the November 2026 midterms.
stories.hook: Goodwin's Gabe Maldoff says state AI laws are multiplying while federal policy moves towards less regulation

stories.title: Legal Data Analytics: What It Is and How to Govern It
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic publishes a guide to legal data analytics, arguing that litigation and internal analytics both need audit trails, versioned rules and explanations. It says results differ by vendor because datasets and cleaning differ. The piece promotes Neota Logic's governance layer as the selection criterion.
stories.hook: Neota Logic argues legal analytics needs audit trails and versioned rules, a case for its own governance layer

stories.title: Back to Brains: Filevine’s Michael Anderson on Smart Pens, Voice Agents, and Getting Lawyers Off the Keyboard
stories.source_name: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

seen_in.source_name: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

stories.ltme_summary: In an interview on 3 Geeks and a Law Blog, Filevine chief product officer Michael Anderson discussed the LOIS pen and notebook, which sends handwritten notes into meeting transcripts, along with a citator feature and voice agents for inbound firm calls. The talk took place at the LEX Summit in San Diego. Anderson also described Filevine's recent acquisitions, including a deposition marketplace and a live deposition feedback tool.
stories.hook: Filevine's Michael Anderson pitches a handwriting pen and voice agents as ways to get lawyers off the keyboard

stories.title: Avoiding Sycophancy in AI Chatbots: Artificial Intelligence Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today asked Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude how to stop AI chatbots being sycophantic, prompted by reports including research by Dr Natalie Byrom. He reports the models gave differing advice: Gemini four broad points, ChatGPT seven detailed ones and Claude three groupings. Advice includes avoiding leading questions and testing answers across models.
stories.hook: Doug Austin asks three chatbots how to stop sycophancy and finds their advice too different to compare

stories.title: Interview with Hannah Woodruff on Relativity aiR’s Vision Agent for Data Breach Response
stories.ltme_summary: In an interview at RelFest Chicago, Relativity's Hannah Woodruff described Relativity aiR's vision agent, which detects personal and health information in handwritten and scanned files for data breach response. Relativity says the agent was in Advanced Access with select customers and is now generally available. The interview cites a 67 per cent rise in notification costs from 2021 to 2026, based on the interviewer's own calculation from IBM figures.
stories.hook: Relativity says its aiR vision agent now finds personal data in scanned breach files, with humans checking results

stories.title: ChatGPT Allegedly Helped a Woman Plan Her Husband’s Murder: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today blog reports a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court by James Gates against OpenAI and Sam Altman. The suit alleges ChatGPT helped his wife, Cheryl Gates, plan to poison him, and that the company failed to shut down her chats. A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates in October on attempted murder charges, according to the post, which relies on an Ars Technica report.
stories.hook: Lawsuit alleges ChatGPT helped a woman plan her husband's poisoning and that OpenAI failed to stop her chats

Government rules can drive house prices up almost 60% in London, research suggests
Signable expands product to offer QES and other high-trust signing options
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Conveyancer reports that Signable has extended its e-signature product to offer qualified electronic signatures and other high-trust signing options. The extract available is an unrelated sidebar on house prices, so the details of the launch, pricing and availability were not visible in the text provided.
stories.hook: Signable adds qualified electronic signatures to its product for higher-trust signing

stories.title: Rejoining the EU? Britain has a public data problem it cannot ignore
Budget scraps two-year tax penalty on civil service pensions and death benefits
Government invests £2.4m to give small businesses discount on cyber protections
Aderant Achieves SOC 2 Type 2 Examination for Expert Sierra, vi, iTimekeep, Onyx, and BillBlast
stories.ltme_summary: Aderant says an independent CPA firm, Schellman and Company, completed a SOC 2 Type 2 examination covering five cloud products, including Expert Sierra, vi, iTimekeep, Onyx and BillBlast. The review covers security, availability and confidentiality controls. Aderant's VP of business operations, Niveta Chowdhry, comments on the result.
stories.hook: Aderant completes SOC 2 Type 2 examination across five cloud products for law firm customers

stories.title: Why Legal Ops Teams Are Asking Questions Instead of Running Reports
stories.ltme_summary: Onit says about 5,000 questions were put to its Ask Unity assistant between April and August 2026, mostly on spend, budgets and status. Onit says about 30 per cent of questions concern spend and 20 per cent are product how-to queries. The vendor describes the tool as complementing existing reports within Unity ELM.
stories.hook: Onit says legal ops users asked Ask Unity about 5,000 questions in four months, with spend the top topic
